'''Henry "Trae" Winter''' (born March 31, 1972) is an American solar physicist currently employed by the [[Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory]].<ref name="sunloop">{{cite web |title=Sun's Loops are Displaying an Optical Illusion |url=https://www.cfa.harvard.edu/news/2013-18 |website=www.cfa.harvard.edu/ |accessdate=10 September 2018 |language=en |date=30 September 2013}}</ref><ref name="WGBH">{{cite web |last1=Herwick III |first1=Edgar B. |title=How One Astrophysicist Is Helping The Blind 'See' Monday's Solar Eclipse |url=https://www.wgbh.org/news/2017/08/16/science-and-technology/how-one-astrophysicist-helping-blind-see-mondays-solar-eclipse |website=News |publisher=WGBH |accessdate=10 September 2018 |language=en |date=16 August 2017}}</ref> He has carried out data analysis for the [[Solar and Heliospheric Observatory]], [[Yohkoh]], [[Hinode (satellite)|Hinode]], [[Solar Dynamics Observatory|SDO]], and [[TRACE]] spacecraft, but is especially noted for his extensive science education and outreach activities. Outreach activity includes development of several museum exhibits in the [[Boston]] area, and of the "Solar Wall" exhibition at the [[Smithsonian Air and Space Museum]] in [[Washington, D.C.]]
